prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, the principle that a small molecule can induce proximity between a chosen protein and a ubiquitin ligase so that the cell destroys it

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: B052 for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The round-1 record shows that the committee has no majority anywhere, so I am judging on the science. Targeted protein degradation is the one shortlisted achievement whose novelty is a transferable molecular principle rather than a platform: a small molecule induces proximity to an E3 ligase and converts occupancy-driven inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal. Crews and Deshaies established the heterobifunctional concept and showed it works in cells, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target gave the molecular-glue strand its mechanism. In answer to the chair's own question, I would write the citation around the single principle of induced proximity and not list two lineages, so the citation does not blur who discovered what. The mechanism is validated by structures, kinetics and independent laboratories, and the quantitative description of ternary-complex cooperativity is the kind of physical underpinning I look for. The absence of an approved PROTAC should weigh less than the validated mechanism, but I would not defend the prize on the pipeline.
statement.case_against: Maturity and attribution remain real weaknesses. No PROTAC drug is approved, although cereblon-directed glues are already in the clinic, and a committee that wants a completed therapeutic record can reasonably wait. Ciulli (rational VHL ligand design), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are excluded by the three-person limit, and Chabes is right that the Ciulli case is strong. The PROTAC and glue lineages are historically separate, and Handa's cereblon work is closer to the glue lineage than to the PROTAC concept, so the trio is a compromise rather than an obviously natural unit. Finally, only two of us configured B052, so I cannot claim a mandate.

responses.point: Aili configures B052 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and writes a citation naming both PROTACs and cereblon-directed glues, while accepting that no PROTAC is approved and that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are left out.
responses.response: We now hold the same trio. I still prefer a citation that states one principle, induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, over one that names two technologies, because the latter invites the objection that we are crediting two prizes inside one. On clinical maturity I agree with him that the mechanism is the discovery, but I take it less lightly than he does: I would be more comfortable if cereblon-directed agents already in patients are cited as the proof that the principle works in humans. His point about base editing and the 2020 CRISPR prize is fair and it contributed to my staying with B052.

responses.point: Chabes configures B055 for Balasubramanian and Klenerman paired with B021 for Liu alone, and asks for Ciulli in any B052 trio.
responses.response: I have taken the two-part prize seriously, but I do not move to it. Sequencing remains exceptionally mature, yet he concedes that it risks reading as an enabling instrument technology, and the Rothberg, Ju and Mayer claims are unresolved. Pairing it with Liu alone for base editing also asks the committee to settle the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo question by omission. On Ciulli, I accept that his VHL ligand work is a fine chemical contribution, but the concept and its first cellular demonstration belong to Crews and Deshaies, and I do not see which of the three he would replace. Handa is the weakest fit for a PROTAC-only citation, which is why I want the citation to be about induced proximity.

responses.point: Zou moves to B055 for the Cambridge pair, treats Rothberg's 454 work as displaced, and calls B052 the stronger alternative if the committee wants a molecular principle rather than an engineered platform.
responses.response: I agree with his reasoning on Rothberg and have dropped it from my own thinking, and I welcome that he names B052 as the principle-based alternative. That is the criterion I am applying. Where we differ is that he regards the missing priority picture for sequencing as something he cannot verify, and a prize whose attribution the committee cannot defend is a weaker prize. If his concern is category, a plain chemistry citation for reversible terminators for the Cambridge pair is possible, but it would still need an answer on Ju and Mayer, and I do not think that answer is currently in hand.

responses.point: Somfai configures B031 for Hartwig and Buchwald, argues for breadth of use in synthesis, and flags the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precedent.
responses.response: I respect that he says plainly that his case rests on breadth of use and not on a new principle. That is the part I cannot get past. A prize for a mature reaction would be deserved but would be read as the follow-on to 2010, and he himself lists Kosugi as unverified. I would still rank it above several candidates on attribution, which is clean. If it were the only way to reach five votes I would not block it, but I would ask him whether the ligand-design principle is demonstrably distinct from the 2010 work in what it taught chemists.

responses.point: Aqvist configures B007 for Car and Parrinello on clean two-person priority, and lists B052 as an alternative while asking whether the Crews, Deshaies, Handa split is defensible.
responses.response: His attribution argument is the strongest on the shortlist, and I answered the one-sentence citation question in my round-1 reply: first-principles dynamics where forces are computed from the electronic structure on the fly. My remaining worry is that he himself names the overlap with the 1998 prize and the fact that current practice often uses Born-Oppenheimer propagation, which leaves the Car-Parrinello-specific claim narrower than the concept. On B052, I think the split is defensible if we credit the principle of induced proximity, with Crews and Deshaies for the concept and Handa for the cereblon mechanism that explains glues.

uncertainties: Whether Handa can be defended as part of a citation about induced proximity or whether the committee prefers Ciulli in his place.
Whether the committee will weigh the absence of an approved PROTAC drug more heavily than I do.
Whether a prize would be read as favouring a drug-discovery pipeline in a year when the opening vote did not converge.
Whether base editing (B021) or sequencing (B055) would command a majority if their attribution questions were settled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict. I am at Lund University, as are Somfai and Sparr, but no shortlisted candidate is a Lund colleague or collaborator, and my own work on nanowire thermoelectrics and molecular motors does not overlap with any shortlisted topic. Nothing has changed since round 1.
